title: US average price of electricity per kilowatt-hour, October 2026
made_at_note: evidence.json, which holds the forecast, was written at this time (UTC)
sealed_at_note: written by our own machine; the independent date is the OpenTimestamps proof bls-electricity-price-2026-10-seal.json.ots
code_note: the commit of the private code repository that built the seal and the one that ran the evidence; the seal's numbers recompute from its inputs either way

series.name: Average price: electricity per kilowatt-hour in U.S. city average
series.program: Consumer Price Index, average price data

target.release_basis: announced: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm (published with the CPI: 'October 2026 / Nov. 10, 2026 / 08:30 AM')

vintage.note: Average prices are not seasonally adjusted and are not routinely revised; the next CPI release (2026-12-10) is the bound.

notes: Summer-peaking seasonality: the ETS member fits a seasonal term and seasonal naive joins the ensemble (the default for a monthly series that is not seasonally adjusted).
Published to a tenth of a cent ($0.196), so one printed step is about half a percent.
claim_rule: 'sealed before publication' only if the OpenTimestamps attestation's block time precedes the release; a seal attested on or after the release is void

selection.rule: Serve the method with the lowest out-of-time MAE over the backtest origins. Where the ensemble's MAE gap to that method has a 95% interval (moving-block bootstrap of origins) that holds zero, serve the ensemble. If the method served is the random walk, the target is not sealed: the model adds nothing over repeating the last value.
selection.basis: random_walk has the lowest MAE; the ensemble's gap to it, +0.000334 (95% interval -0.000026 to +0.000796), holds zero

method.selection_rule: Serve the method with the lowest out-of-time MAE over the backtest origins. Where the ensemble's MAE gap to that method has a 95% interval (moving-block bootstrap of origins) that holds zero, serve the ensemble. If the method served is the random walk, the target is not sealed: the model adds nothing over repeating the last value.

point.seasonal_naive: the value one season before the target
point.drift: the last value plus h times the mean change over the fit window
point.ets: damped-trend exponential smoothing, weights from a fixed grid by the least in-sample one-step squared error
point.ensemble_mean: the mean of random_walk, seasonal_naive, drift, ets on the log scale (a geometric mean)

method.bands: split-conformal, every method its own: the point plus or minus the ceil((n+1)*level)-th smallest absolute 1-step-ahead residual of that method over its newest 60 rolling-origin backtest origins, on the log scale

scoring_plan: Target: Average price: electricity per kilowatt-hour in U.S. city average (APU000072610), 2026-10, as published by U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and read from https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=APU000072610.

Value scored against: the first print: the value U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes for 2026-10 on release day, read from the spec's URL on or after the release and before 2026-12-10, when the next release may revise it. The scorer records the value, the retrieval time and the sha256 of the raw response. Vintage note: Average prices are not seasonally adjusted and are not routinely revised; the next CPI release (2026-12-10) is the bound.
Not scored, with the reason, if the period is not published by 2027-05-11, if it was published before this seal's OpenTimestamps attestation, or if the series is redefined.

Metric: absolute error in U.S. dollars per kilowatt-hour for the served forecast (ensemble_mean, the headline) and for every other sealed method, the three baselines (random walk, seasonal naive, drift) among them; whether the published value falls inside each method's sealed 80% and 95% bands; the interval score at both levels. Published to 3 decimal place(s), so the published value carries up to half a unit of rounding in its last place.
Claim: 'sealed before publication' when the attestation's block time precedes the release.
